data.description: Found in the AS-106 review (qa-priya, 2026-09-11). The AS-106 plan §2(b)4 says the always-down teardown runs 'on SIGINT/SIGTERM (the trap … EXIT of the shell recipe, in node)', and §5 treats T5c (exec stub throws) as the proxy for that path. It is not one: bin/compose-run.mjs registers no signal handler and drives docker with spawnSync, so a signal to the node process ends it before any JS can run. Observed for real (scratchpad/agent-qa-priya/AS-106/sig.mjs): SIGTERM to the script mid-container -> node exits with signal=SIGTERM, prints nothing (no receipt), the compose child runs on and --rm removes only the container; asc-review-as106-sigterm_default and asc-review-as106-sigterm-test:latest survived until a hand 'down -v --rmi local --remove-orphans'. With the AS-106 network_mode: none pin the chat suite leaks only its image this way; any other compose dir (T11's shape) leaks a network too. This is the tick-timeout / harness-termination case in real operation. Fix shape (implementer's call): ignore SIGINT/SIGTERM in the parent for the duration of the run (process.on(sig, noop) before spawnSync, remove after) so the child's termination surfaces as a non-zero status and the existing always-down path runs; add a real-signal test (opt-in, AS106_REAL style) whose falsifier is 'remove the handler -> the network survives'. Not blocking AS-106: AC-5 names exit 0 / exit 1 / throw and all three hold; the plan itself de-scoped a real-signal test.
data.title: Chat tooling: compose-run.mjs does not tear down on SIGINT/SIGTERM — an interrupted counted run leaves its image (and, off the pinned compose, its network) behind

data.body: Implemented on feat/AS-121-compose-run-signals (tip 449571c), plan .lattice/plans/task_01M29CJ6AGQ3ZQXDRX5FQDYKQ9.md. Kept low: one production file (bin/compose-run.mjs), the filed fix shape. For the counted run only, SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers record the first signal; spawnSync defers the callback so the process survives, the compose child ends (with the group, or to completion on parent-only delivery), and runCounted's always-down path runs unchanged. main() yields one setImmediate turn so the deferred handler fires before reporting; an interrupted run prints 'compose-run: interrupted by <SIG> ... not a receipt' on stderr and exits 128+signum when the lib exit was 0 (a non-zero lib exit is kept). README paragraph added. Tests: T12a (parent-only SIGTERM, Priya's shape) and T12b (group SIGINT via detached + kill(-pid)) spawn the real script against a #!/bin/sh stub docker as ADVANCE_DOCKER_BIN; T13 is the real-docker variant under the file's existing AS106_REAL=1 switch. Receipts: host branch 627/624/0/3; compose asc-impl-as121 'Image asc-impl-as121-test Built' 627/618/0/9 leak check clean (master was 624/616/0/8: +3 tests, +2 pass, +1 skipped = exactly T12a/T12b/T13); real T13 pass, leftover scan clean. Mutants in place with backup/restore, mutation asserted applied: M1 (drop handlers) red {T12a,T12b} EXACT; M2 (drop 128+signum) red {T12a} EXACT; M3 (drop setImmediate yield) red {T12a,T12b} EXACT; git diff --exit-code 0 after restore, post-restore green. Left undone, recorded as a non-goal: the signal is not forwarded to the compose child, so a parent-only SIGTERM waits for the container before tearing down; doing that needs runCounted async in lib/compose-run.js (second production file) — follow-up if the watcher's 15 s SIGTERM->SIGKILL grace matters. SIGKILL is unreachable. AS-122: untouched, neither easier nor harder (this adds nothing to the leak-check path). Battery: scratchpad/agent-developer-lena/AS-121/ (battery.mjs, real-t13.mjs, logs, receipt).

REVIEW AS-121 (qa-priya, cold: plan + diff @ 449571c; implementer comment and daemon output not read).

FINDINGS (2 outside the list; 1 blocks)
F1 — BLOCKS (implementation-level, behaviour): the handler is registered before `runCounted`, which contains observe/preflight/guard, so a SIGINT/SIGTERM arriving during `network ls`/`compose ls` (before the run) is swallowed and the `compose run --build` then STARTS. Observed with a stub docker sleeping on `network ls`: SIGTERM at that point -> run, down, exit 143, stderr "interrupted … during the run" (false — it was before). Plan §2.1 "not before the guard", AC-4 "a signal before the run still terminates by default", and the new README sentence all claim otherwise. Consequence under the watcher's 15 s SIGTERM->SIGKILL: a tick-cutoff signal in that window starts a multi-minute build that is then SIGKILLed — the original leak. Fix shape is the implementer's; a bin-only one is to install the handler in the `exec` wrapper only when argv includes `run` (keep the post-run yield + off in main), and correct the README/stderr wording. Add a stub test (sleep on `network ls`, expect death by signal, no `run` line).
R1 — residual, not blocking (test hygiene): when the script dies mid-container (M1 under AS106_REAL), T13's `t.after` `down` races the still-running container and leaves `<project>_default` + `<project>-test` behind (attributed by timestamp; removed by hand). Fold into the next task touching this file.
Probes that held: three signals mid-run -> survives all, first wins, 130; `--check` under SIGTERM dies by default.

FLOOR CHECK (criteria sweep, after findings): AC-1 pass, AC-2 pass, AC-3 pass, AC-5 pass (T13 real, 12.2 s, zero networks/images), AC-4 FAIL on the "signal before the run terminates by default" clause (F1); T1–T11 green, `--check` clause holds. 4/5.

NUMBERS: host suite in worktree 627 tests / 624 pass / 0 fail / 3 skipped. AS106_REAL=1 compose-run file: 19/19 (T11, T13 live). Counted run `-p asc-review-as121` receipt: `Image asc-review-as121-test Built`, tests=627 pass=618 fail=0 skipped=9, run 0 / down 0 / leak check clean / exit 0. Mutants (scratch worktree, each asserted at site, restored, diff clean): M1 red {T12a,T12b,T13} = plan; M2 red {T12a} = plan; M3 red {T12a,T12b} = plan.

Left behind: nothing (scratch worktree removed; asc-review-as121 / asc-as121-real-* / asc-probe-* all gone). Logs, receipts, probe.mjs, probe-out.txt: scratchpad/agent-qa-priya/AS-121/.

VERDICT: implementation-level rework (F1).
